def: A curated, versioned set of items with trusted answers and a fixed scoring rule, designed so different systems and dates can be compared.
A short document defining what a benchmark measures: the input, output, scoring rule, scope and the decision the score feeds.
One case in a benchmark: an input, any context it needs, and the information required to score a response.
A grid of the dimensions along which questions differ, with the number of items planned and found in each cell.
The trusted answer, accepted variants or checking rule against which a response to an item is scored.
The share of systems or attempts that get an item right in a pilot run.
How well an item separates stronger systems from weaker ones, often measured as its correlation with the total score on the other items.
A statistical framework that models the chance of solving an item from the system's ability and the item's difficulty.
A division of benchmark items into a visible set for tuning and a rarely used held-out set for reporting.
Structured documentation of a dataset's purpose, sources, labelling, composition, limits and intended use.
A fingerprint of a dataset's exact contents, used to show that two scores came from the same version.
The score domain experts achieve on a benchmark under the same conditions, which shows how much headroom exists.
